newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says RBNZ target no longer respectable.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says RBNZ target no longer respectable.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday that the Reserve Bank's zero to two percent underlying inflation target was no longer "respectable".

Peters was critical of both the existing range, supported by the caretaker National Party government, and Labour's proposal to widen it to minus one to three percent. He noted the mid-point of the range was the same in each case.
"The reality is the National and Labour Party have the same mid-point focus with respect to the Reserve Bank Act," Peters told a news conference.

"Sure, they have got the same policy that the Reserve Bank governor is targeting. It's a target that I think even the Reserve Bank governor does not find respectable any more. I think he would tend more to support New Zealand First's stance with respect to the inflation target," Peters said.

New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power between Labour and National, wants to make the central bank aim for inflation below the average of New Zealand's main trading partners. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
